title: LIBERNIUM 2026
venue: CHRIST (Deemed to be University), Bangalore Bannerghatta Road Campus
tagline: Building a Sustainable Future Through Conscious Choices
about: Libernium, organised by the Department of Liberal Arts, is an annual flagship interdisciplinary event that engages with themes such as sustainability, zero-waste living, cultural studies, and regional development. This year's edition centres on responsible consumption and production through workshops, artisan demonstrations and a panel discussion.
objectives: Facilitate experiential and interdisciplinary learning on sustainability and zero-waste living.
Enable students to critically examine everyday consumption practices and production systems through structured, activity-based learning formats.
Promote skill-based learning in traditional and contemporary craft practices as a means of understanding sustainable production and material reuse.
Extend sustainability education through experiential learning alongside the Department's conference tradition.

paragraphs: Libernium, organised by the Department of Liberal Arts, is an annual flagship interdisciplinary event that engages with themes such as sustainability, zero-waste living, cultural studies, and regional development. As part of this year's edition, the Department chose a theme ‘Responsible Consumption and Production’, centred on workshops, competitions, and a panel discussion.

The theme examines consumption not simply as an economic act but as a cultural practice, shaped by production systems, everyday habits, and the ways societies use, discard, and revalue what they make and buy. Centred on this idea, the event brings together artisans, practitioners, and academicians to encourage students to engage critically and creatively with sustainable practices through discussion, collaboration, and experiential learning.
The event follows a one-day experiential format: the day features hands-on workshops that introduce students to sustainable practices and creative approaches to responsible consumption.
objectives: Facilitate experiential and interdisciplinary learning on sustainability and zero-waste living.
Enable students to critically examine everyday consumption practices and production systems through structured, activity-based learning formats.
Promote skill-based learning in traditional and contemporary craft practices as a means of understanding sustainable production and material reuse.
Extend the Department's ongoing engagement with sustainability education by broadening Libernium's format to include experiential-based learning alongside its conference tradition.
